To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MCNPX is a useful tool for simulating CT dose and that the ICRP adult voxel phantoms provide a significant improvement on the MIRD stylised phantoms.

1) MCNPX is an effective tool for simulating photon transport and energy depositions in anthropomorphic phatoms; 2) the ICRP adult voxel phantoms are more realistic than the MIRD stylized hermaphrodites, but the voxel phantoms require more time to calculate organ and effective doses; 3) the organ dose results from the ICRP phantoms are not consistent with those from the MIRD phantoms; 4
the use of voxel phantoms in place of the mathematical phantoms used in the ImPACT tool leads to significantly different organ and effective doses for a range of CT scanner models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of computational modelling techniques for the assessment of radiation dose in CT.

the development of a new generation of computational phantoms for radiation protection and medical physics applications, the validation of these phantoms, and the application of the phantoms to the calculation of radiation doses to organs and tissue from CT scanners.
the calculation of organ doses and effective dose to the AM and AF phantoms from contemporary CT scanners.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of the voxel phantoms in the MCNPX simulations has provided more realistic results than the use of the MIRD phantoms.
the use of the voxel phantoms in place of the stylised hermophrodite mathematical phan- toms is a major step forward in CT dose estimation.
the ICRP AM and AF voxel phantoms are more anatomically representative than the stylised MIRD phantoms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the value of using voxel phantoms in the simulation of organ doses from CT scans.
MCNPX is a useful and powerful code for the Monte Carlo simulation of CT scanners and the dose to phantoms.
the MCNPX code is capable of simulating the photon transport and energy absorption in the AM and AF phantoms with a high degree of accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the voxel phantoms are a significant improvement on the MIRD mathematical phantoms and that they should be used in future studies of CT dose.
the use of a realistic anthropomorphic phantom for CT dose calculations can lead to significant differences in results compared to a stylised hermophrodite mathematical phantom.
the ICRP AM and AF voxel phantoms are more realistic than the MIRD mathematical phantoms and should be used for dose simulations.
